attributes.action: Cap headlight colour temperature as well as brightness to reduce glare
attributes.additional_details:
That commissioned research must now be turned into an actual regulatory standard.

Older drivers and people with astigmatism can be affected even more severely, as glare sensitivity increases with age — this problem can only grow as the population ages. In 2016, medical guidance led to a colour temperature cap for street lighting. Headlights sit at eye level and cause more direct, severe glare than streetlights — any new limit must be set specifically for vehicles, not simply copied from streetlight standards.
attributes.background: We want the Government to cap the maximum colour temperature of vehicle headlights, not just their brightness. The DfT commissioned TRL research confirming headlight glare is a real problem: 96% of drivers surveyed said headlights are too bright & a third have stopped or reduced driving at night.
